prompt: Should a 10-minute grocery delivery company launch in Tier-2 cities like Indore and Coimbatore? How would you decide?

hiddenFacts: Company goal if asked: reach profitability in 18 months; currently profitable in 4 of 7 metros.
Tier-2 differences if asked: lower order density, lower AOV, cheaper rent and labour, strong local kirana loyalty.

expectedStructure: Clarify the objective (growth versus profitability) and decision criteria
Unit economics: order density, AOV, cost per order
Customer: need for 10-minute delivery in Tier-2
Options (launch, pilot one city, adapt to 30 minutes), recommendation, risks, pilot metrics

rubricHints.structure: Objective, then criteria, then options, then recommendation.
rubricHints.userFocus: Questions whether Tier-2 customers need 10 minutes.
rubricHints.prioritisation: Makes a call (for example pilot one city) with explicit criteria.
rubricHints.metrics: Pilot success metrics like orders per store per day and contribution margin per order by month 3.

commonPitfalls: Pure framework recital with no decision

followUpSeeds.text: Bottom line: launch, don't, or something else? Commit to one.
If you pilot, what numbers at month 3 make you expand or shut it down?
Does a family in Indore actually need groceries in 10 minutes? What's your evidence?
New fact: {variant}. Does your recommendation change?

constraint: the company must cut cash burn by 40% this year
market: the target is Dhaka, not Indian Tier-2 cities
user: a competitor already launched in both cities 6 months ago

prompt: Should a UPI app launch credit products for college students?

context.setup: You're the head of lending at a large UPI app.
hiddenFacts: Company goal if asked: grow credit revenue without raising defaults beyond 3%.
About 4 crore students in India; most have no credit history and rely on parents' money.
A partner NBFC would bear the credit risk but takes most of the margin.
Regulation requires clear consent and limits on marketing to minors; many students are under 21.

expectedStructure: Clarify the objective and the risk appetite
Customer: why students would borrow and what for
Economics: ticket size, repayment, default, cost to acquire
Options: launch, pilot with parent co-sign, partner with colleges, skip
Recommendation with criteria; risks and regulation

rubricHints.structure: Frames a decision rather than a market overview.
rubricHints.userFocus: Distinguishes students who need small emergency credit from those chasing consumption.
rubricHints.prioritisation: Chooses an option and says what is not done.
rubricHints.metrics: Default rate by cohort, repayment on time, cost of acquisition per active borrower.

followUpSeeds.text: Pick one: launch, pilot, or skip. Why?
What default rate would make you stop the pilot?
Who is the student who benefits here, and who could be harmed?
Suppose {variant}. Does your recommendation change?

constraint: the partner NBFC will only lend to students with a parent co-signer
market: the segment is young working professionals instead of students

prompt: Should a Bengaluru-based pharmacy delivery startup expand to Hyderabad next?

hiddenFacts: Company goal if asked: reach 3x orders in 12 months while keeping delivery under 45 minutes.

expectedStructure: Compare markets on demand, competition, regulation
Options: enter, pilot, partner with chemists, defer

rubricHints.userFocus: Differentiates chronic-care repeat users from emergency buyers.
rubricHints.metrics: Orders per store, repeat rate and delivery time targets.

followUpSeeds.text: Decide: enter, pilot or wait?
What numbers after 90 days tell you to continue?
Which customers will you win first?

prompt: Assume you lead product at the number two UPI app, and the number one app's share keeps growing. What do you do?

hiddenFacts: If asked: UPI P2P and P2M transactions earn almost no direct revenue; money comes from adjacent services (credit, insurance, ads, merchant tools).
If asked: a market-share cap regulation has been discussed but not enforced.
Your company's strength: a large search and ads business and strong Android distribution.

expectedStructure: Clarify the real objective: share for its own sake or monetisable engagement
Diagnose why number one is winning (merchant QR network, habits, features)
Options: compete head-on, differentiate on adjacent value, merchant play, partnerships

rubricHints.structure: Diagnosis before options; options before recommendation.
rubricHints.userFocus: Understands both consumer habit and merchant acceptance.
rubricHints.prioritisation: Picks a focused bet and says what not to do.
rubricHints.metrics: Metrics beyond share: monthly transacting users, merchant activations, adjacent revenue per user.

commonPitfalls: Cashback wars as the main answer
No diagnosis of why number one wins

followUpSeeds.text: Is market share even the right goal here, given UPI itself makes little money?
Before solutions: why is the number one app winning?
In 12 months, which three numbers prove your strategy is working?
Now assume {variant}. What changes?

constraint: the 30% market-share cap will be enforced in 6 months
market: the same situation in Indonesia's QRIS ecosystem
